name: Wells by District (Minor Irrigation Census 2017-18)
description: Wells per LGD district from the 6th Minor Irrigation Census (reference year 2017-18): dugwells and shallow, medium and deep tubewells, with status, pump energy source, depth and irrigation potential. Official census counts summed to districts.
source_org: Minor Irrigation (Statistics) Wing, Ministry of Jal Shakti
notes: Counts from the 6th Minor Irrigation Census (reference year 2017-18, enumerated 2019-22), Minor Irrigation (Statistics) Wing, Ministry of Jal Shakti, published on data.gov.in under GODL-India. Summed from the ground-water scheme files to LGD districts by Land Ledger; the total matches the census report (21,931,924 wells). Census districts are the 2017-18 ones: districts carved out since have no counts of their own (status new_district) and their former district keeps them (counts_pre_split); counts are not split. Irrigation potential utilised is gross, summed over seasons, not net irrigated area. Depth classes are bins of the reported scheme depth. Well locations are not published and nothing below the district is included here. Delhi, Ladakh, Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu were not in the census; Manipur and Sikkim report no ground-water schemes. Map tiles rebaked by bharatlas with the popup fields only; every column is in the parquet and the downloads.

Both names are kept (ulbnm from SBM, cf_ulb_name from CityFinance); where they differ, SBM's label is the one that is off (e.g. Bapatla's polygon is named GUNTUR in SBM). Source: "State/UT-wise Details of Per Capita Net State Domestic Product at Current Prices from 2019-20 to 2022-23", Rajya Sabha session 262, starred question 94, answered 11 December 2023; data as on 01-08-2023 (data.gov.in resource c9bfd3c0-b9de-4a5b-8752-f72a4f2932ad). outstanding_liabilities_pct_gsdp_mar_2021_actual, outstanding_liabilities_pct_gsdp_mar_2023_be: total outstanding liabilities of the state government as percent of GSDP at end-March, 2021 actual and 2023 budget estimate (states and UTs with a legislature only). Source: "State/UT-wise Details of Total Outstanding Liabilities of States & UT with Legislature as Percent of (GSDP) from 2021 to 2023", Rajya Sabha session 260, unstarred question 1353, answered 1 August 2023; RBI, State Finances: A Study of Budgets of 2022-23 (data.gov.in resource b53abcb0-fcb2-4de9-82d5-6df1cd2a6306). gst_gross_2023_24_rs_crore: gross GST collection on domestic supplies, 2023-24 (the latest full year; the table's 2024-25 runs only to October 2024), Rs crore. Source: "State/UT-wise Details of Gross Goods and Service Tax (GST) Collection from 2020-21 to 2024-25", Rajya Sabha session 266, unstarred question 881, answered 3 December 2024 (data.gov.in resource 5d0b81aa-d513-4dfd-9f57-84571829c049). direct_tax_gross_2022_23_rs_crore: gross direct tax collection, 2022-23, Rs crore, placed by the state code of the assessing officer's jurisdiction (so states hosting company head offices, such as Maharashtra and Delhi, carry tax earned elsewhere). name: Railway stations
description: One point per Indian Railways station or halt, with its station code, merged by bharatlas from two government copies of the CRIS station layer (PM GatiShakti and the IR GIS portal) and Wikidata station codes, with a source and match-confidence column on every row.
source_org: Indian Railways (CRIS), via PM GatiShakti and the IR GIS portal; Wikidata
notes: Merged by bharatlas and published under CC BY 4.0 (credit: bharatlas, Indian Railways / CRIS, PM GatiShakti, Wikidata). Sources: (1) PM GatiShakti railway stations (BISAG-N), drawn from CRIS's Indian Railways station layer; (2) the Indian Railways GIS portal stations (irgeoportal.gov.in, CRIS), the ir_stations layer; both compiled by ramSeraph/indianopenmaps (DataMeet community, CC0 1.0) and republished with credit under bharatlas.com/about#sources-and-licensing; (3) Wikidata items with an Indian Railways station code (P5696), CC0 1.0. Every location comes from CRIS. CRIS records most stations as several points (start, centre, end, platforms); points sharing a station code become one row at their medoid, and uncoded points within 1 km fold into it (source_points counts them, source_spread_m is how far they spread). Points of one code more than 2 km apart are treated as different stations. GatiShakti is used first; the IR portal adds the 52 codes GatiShakti lacks. A Wikidata code missing from CRIS is placed on the nearest CRIS station within 1.5 km whose name or description agrees (match_method name+distance; this also links CRIS's older codes to the current ones, e.g. CSTM/CSMT, BCT/MMCT, HNZM/NZM, KEU/KIUL: stn_code keeps CRIS's code, code holds Wikidata's), or on an uncoded CRIS point within 500 m on distance alone (distance). match_confidence: high = CRIS code and Wikidata agree within 1 km; medium = CRIS code not in Wikidata or 1 to 2 km away, or a name-confirmed match; low = Wikidata more than 2 km away, a distance-only match, or an uncoded CRIS point (stn_code empty). Checked against OpenStreetMap: high rows sit a median 26 m from OSM's station with the same code (98% within 500 m), medium 90%, low 87%. OpenStreetMap is used only for that check and is not merged, because its ODbL licence would require the whole layer to stay under ODbL. Every source column is kept as published (sttncode, sttnname, fdetail ... from CRIS; item, code, coord, label from Wikidata; coord is Wikidata's point, kept for reference, never the location), except the CRIS GIS accounts that created and last edited each point (created_us, last_edite), left out because some are individuals' usernames. Known gaps: about 800 Wikidata codes have no CRIS point to sit on and are left out (e.g. Kalyan KYN, whose only CRIS point is coded THK, and Lokmanya Tilak Terminus LTT); Wikidata positions are mostly copied from the 2016 datameet/railways compilation and sit a median ~90 m and a 90th percentile ~1.2 km from CRIS, so they are not used as locations. About 300 rows are uncoded, unnamed CRIS points. CRIS state names are as published (mixed case, some blank). Map tiles rebaked by bharatlas with the popup fields only; every column is in the parquet and the downloads.

name: Water Bodies (1st Census, 2017-18)
description: Ponds, tanks, lakes, reservoirs and check dams from the 1st Census of Water Bodies (reference year 2017-18): one point per water body with its type, ownership, use, storage, water spread, encroachment and repair or revival schemes.
source_org: Minor Irrigation (Statistics) Wing, Ministry of Jal Shakti
notes: Incomplete: this layer holds 1,101,912 of the 2,424,540 water bodies the 1st Census of Water Bodies counted, because its source, the data.gov.in API of the 1st Water Bodies Census, holds fewer for some States. Partial States: Andhra Pradesh 21,052 of 190,777; Assam 72,119 of 172,492; Odisha 61,802 of 181,837; Uttar Pradesh 41,435 of 245,087; West Bengal 54,876 of 747,480. Tripura is missing (the census counted 36,239 there). The data is complete for the other 27 States/UTs. 82,338 records without usable coordinates are kept with no geometry (no point on the map). 1st Census of Water Bodies (reference year 2017-18), Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation and the Minor Irrigation (Statistics) Wing, Ministry of Jal Shakti, published per State/UT on data.gov.in under GODL-India and read through its API. Columns are as published ("NA" or "NULL" in a numeric column becomes empty); unique_id holds the census's own state/district/block/village codes, not LGD codes. The point is the enumerator's latitude_dec/longitude_dec as published (the manual asks for the north-west corner of the water body); many were keyed in by hand and some are stacked on one spot. Of 1,101,912 records: 1,019,233 fall inside India's bounding box, 341 outside it, 0 at (0,0), 25 have impossible values (beyond 180 degrees longitude or 90 latitude) and 82,313 have no numeric coordinates (32 of them give degrees/minutes/seconds text such as 17/41/29). A registry, not satellite mapping: compare with wris_waterbodies, do not treat them as the same features. Map tiles rebaked by bharatlas with the popup fields only; every column is in the parquet and the downloads.

name: Permeability and porosity (GLHYMPS 2.0)
description: How easily water moves through the ground near the surface (permeability) and how much of it is open space (porosity), mapped as rock and sediment polygons across India, from GLHYMPS 2.0.
notes: GLHYMPS 2.0, the global hydrogeology map of Huscroft, Gleeson, Hartmann and Börker 2018, "Compiling and mapping global permeability of the unconsolidated and consolidated Earth", Geophysical Research Letters 45 (https://doi.org/10.1002/2017GL075860), published on Borealis (https://doi.org/10.5683/SP2/TTJNIU, version 1.0) under CC-BY 4.0. Every polygon that touches India (its boundary as shown on bharatlas, claimed areas included) is kept whole, so some reach past the border; every column is as published, with the shapefile's short names. Permeability is log10 of permeability in m², times 100: logK_Ferr_ (without permafrost) and logK_Ice_x (with permafrost) of -1300 mean 10^-13 m². Higher (less negative) values let water through more easily. For hydraulic conductivity of water in m/s, K = 10^(value/100) x 10^7. Porosity_x is porosity in percent (porosity x 100), K_stdev_x1 the standard deviation of log10 permeability x 100. GUM_K says where the values come from (1 GLHYMPS, 2 the Global Unconsolidated Sediments Map) and 0 marks a polygon with no permeability value, whose permeability columns read 0 as published. Prmfrst is 1 inside the permafrost boundary. The source readme describes every column. The map is global and coarse (half the polygons are under 15 km², the largest cover hundreds of thousands of km²): use it for regional patterns, not for a single site.

name: Water balance by micro-watershed (CoRE Stack, 2017-2025)
description: Yearly water balance for each micro-watershed CoRE Stack has mapped, 2017-18 to 2024-25: rainfall, runoff, evapotranspiration, the change in groundwater and the estimated change in depth to water, with net change over 5-year windows.
notes: Each year column (2017_2018 to 2024_2025, July to June) holds a JSON string with Precipitation, RunOff, ET, DeltaG and G in mm and WellDepth in metres: the water balance is rainfall minus runoff minus evapotranspiration, and WellDepth turns it into a change in depth to water using the aquifer's specific yield (weighted_avg_yeild, spelled as published; some tehsil files name it weighted_a, and a few add their own STATE, District and TEHSIL columns, all kept as published). Net2017_22 to Net2020_25 are the net change in depth to water in metres over each 5-year window; where the aquifer's yield is near zero they run very large (about 110 beyond 1,000 m), as published. CoRE Stack notes this counts only vertical flow, not water moving underground between micro-watersheds. Rainfall is from JAXA GSMaP, evapotranspiration from the FLDAS Noah land surface model (NASA, USGS). CoRE Stack computes this layer itself and publishes it per tehsil on its GeoServer, listed in its tehsil-wise STAC files, under CC-BY-4.0. bharatlas puts every tehsil file together as published: one row per micro-watershed per tehsil file, every column as published, with stac_state, stac_district and stac_tehsil added from the STAC path (CoRE Stack's spelling). A micro-watershed that crosses a tehsil boundary is in each tehsil's file, so the same uid can appear more than once, with values CoRE Stack computed for that tehsil. CoRE Stack covers the tehsils it has computed so far, not all of India. Methods: CoRE Stack's technical manual and code (github.com/core-stack-org).

name: Drought by micro-watershed (CoRE Stack, 2017-2024)
description: Drought weeks for each micro-watershed CoRE Stack has mapped, each monsoon from 2017 to 2022 or 2024: weeks in mild, moderate and severe drought, dry spells, monsoon onset, kharif sown area and weekly rainfall deviation.
notes: CoRE Stack follows the Manual for Drought Management (2016, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare), using CHIRPS rainfall, Landsat vegetation, MODIS crop data and IndiaSAT land cover. Per year: w_no, w_mld, w_mod and w_sev are weeks in no, mild, moderate and severe drought out of t_wks weeks analysed; drlb holds the weekly drought labels (0 none, 1 mild, 2 moderate, 3 severe); frth0 to frth3 and inth0 to inth3 are drought frequency and intensity at thresholds 0 to 3; drysp is dry spell length; m_ons the monsoon onset date; kh_cr kharif cropped area in sq km and pcr_k its percent; columns rdYY-M-D are the rainfall deviation in percent for the week starting that date. Most tehsils run to 2024, about a third stop at 2022, so a later year's columns are empty where a tehsil has no data; the weekly columns differ by tehsil, as published. CoRE Stack computes this layer itself and publishes it per tehsil on its GeoServer, listed in its tehsil-wise STAC files, under CC-BY-4.0. bharatlas puts every tehsil file together as published: one row per micro-watershed per tehsil file, every column as published, with stac_state, stac_district and stac_tehsil added from the STAC path (CoRE Stack's spelling). A micro-watershed that crosses a tehsil boundary is in each tehsil's file, so the same uid can appear more than once, with values CoRE Stack computed for that tehsil. CoRE Stack covers the tehsils it has computed so far, not all of India. Methods: CoRE Stack's technical manual and code (github.com/core-stack-org).

name: Groundwater levels, India-WRIS stations
description: Every India-WRIS groundwater-level monitoring station (CGWB and state ground water departments), with a summary of its manual readings in metres below ground level: first and last reading, the latest pre- and post-monsoon depth and the ten-year pre-monsoon trend.
source_org: India-WRIS (Ministry of Jal Shakti): CGWB and state ground water departments
notes: Stations are the India-WRIS station layer as published: every field, the point from its long and lat (445 stations sit outside India as published). Readings come from the India-WRIS Dataset API: 67,106 of 92,973 stations have manual readings, which end in 2024. Columns added by bharatlas from the manual "MANUAL-Water Level" readings: first_reading and last_reading (dates), n_readings, years_of_record (calendar years with a reading), last_depth_m (the last reading), premonsoon_depth_m and premonsoon_year (the latest year's last March to May reading), postmonsoon_depth_m and postmonsoon_year (the same for October and November), and premonsoon_trend_m_per_yr: the least-squares slope of the yearly pre-monsoon depth over 2015-2024 where at least 5 years have one (trend_n_years says how many); a positive trend means the water table is getting deeper. Depths are metres below ground level, so a larger number is a deeper water table; a negative depth is water above ground, as published. Telemetric stations report every few hours and the API cannot leave those readings out, so bharatlas reads them only for the feed's last week (2026-05-29 to 2026-06-04): telemetry_last_value and telemetry_last_at are the last "GPRS-Water Level" value as the sensor reports it (agencies differ in sign and datum). The API answers a large request unreliably, so bharatlas asks for spans small enough to come back whole; where telemetry still filled a district's answer, its manual readings for that span were read on the days that agency took readings in that State. series_complete is false for those stations, whose series may miss a reading. The 3,476,743 manual readings themselves, with every published field, are a separate Parquet download: https://data.bharatlas.com/water/wris-groundwater-levels/WRIS_Groundwater_Manual_Readings.ab41da73.parquet

City bus stops come from these GTFS feeds (stops only, no timetables): BMTC GTFS (Vonter/bmtc-gtfs), ODbL-1.0, https://github.com/Vonter/bmtc-gtfs; PMPML GTFS (croyla/pmpml-gtfs), MIT-0, https://github.com/croyla/pmpml-gtfs; Mumbai region GTFS (croyla/mumbai-gtfs), MIT-0, https://github.com/croyla/mumbai-gtfs; Ahmedabad GTFS (croyla/amd-gtfs), MIT, https://github.com/croyla/amd-gtfs; CUMTA MTC GTFS (cumta.org), none stated (government data, republished with credit), https://cumta.tn.gov.in/; TGSRTC GTFS, Open Data Telangana (via reclaimchennai/tgsrtc), GODL-India, https://www.tgsrtc.telangana.gov.in/open-data; Kadamba Transport Corporation GTFS (ktclgoa.com), CC-BY-4.0, https://ktclgoa.com/gtfs/; Hubballi-Dharwad BRTS GTFS (croyla/hdbrts-gtfs), MIT, https://github.com/croyla/hdbrts-gtfs; Rajkot Rajpath GTFS (croyla/rrl-gtfs), MIT-0, https://github.com/croyla/rrl-gtfs; Davangere city bus GTFS (croyla/dvg-gtfs), MIT-0, https://github.com/croyla/dvg-gtfs; Calcutta Transport GTFS (arkodeepg/calcutta-transport), ODbL-1.0, https://github.com/arkodeepg/calcutta-transport.
